nodes.label: Modelo LOCAL por sucursal (Windows + PM2, sin nube)
nodes.rationale: One server per branch, fully isolated and Dockerless: it works because only a single branch enters data at a time, so heavy work can run inline inside the request.

nodes.label: Flujo de costo de domicilio (pull → cotiza → writeback)
nodes.rationale: Delivery pulls orders from PEDIDO, computes warehouse→client distance times the formula using the per-SKU weight fetched over the VPN, and writes costoDomicilio back into PEDIDO over HTTP, all scoped to the branch.

nodes.label: Tabla SyncJob como "redis sin redis"
nodes.rationale: A DB table plus a polling worker stands in for a real queue so the local install needs no Redis; it also backs the live /sync page over SSE.

nodes.label: Guard de configuración (fórmula + punto de partida)
nodes.rationale: Quoting refuses to run until both the global formula and the branch warehouse coordinates exist, so jobs queue instead of producing wrong prices; changing either afterwards only affects new orders, leaving already-quoted ones stable.

nodes.label: VPN WireGuard por sucursal (túnel al warehouse)
nodes.rationale: Each server has its own tunnel installed as a service; two tunnels on the same 10.188.2.0/24 must never be active at once because they collide.

nodes.label: Data Warehouse de pesos (10.188.2.2:3001, read-only por VPN)
nodes.rationale: Remote read-only source of per-SKU weightKg reachable only through the VPN; many products lack a weight and are quoted with 0 kg, distance pricing still applies.

nodes.label: SUCURSAL_CODIGO (scoping del worker por sucursal)
nodes.rationale: In the local model it holds this branch's code so the worker only pulls its own orders; in the centralized model it is empty so one worker processes every branch.

nodes.label: Next bajo PM2 no carga .env (set -a; . ./.env; set +a)
nodes.rationale: PM2 spawns the process without Next's dotenv loading, so DATABASE_URL and friends must be exported into the shell environment before pm2 start or the app comes up unconfigured.

nodes.label: Migración SQLite→Postgres con export-all.mjs / import-all.mjs
nodes.rationale: Repo migrations are SQLite-shaped, so Postgres schemas are created with prisma db push and data moves via a JSON dump imported with idempotent upserts by id — no data loss and re-runnable.

nodes.label: Backfill de sucursalId antes de importar geo
nodes.rationale: The geolocation importer matches on sucursalId plus name, so if legacy orders/clients still have NULL sucursalId after the multi-branch migration the import matches nothing (0%). Order matters: backfill first, geo second.

nodes.label: Prisma 7 con driver adapter (prisma-node-client.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Standalone .mjs scripts can no longer construct a bare PrismaClient under Prisma 7; they must go through the driver adapter.

nodes.label: Worker procovar-delivery-sync debe estar online
nodes.rationale: It is a separate PM2 process from the web app; without it orders enqueue but nobody processes them and costoDomicilio is never computed.

nodes.label: delivery se queda en Postgres (campos Json)
nodes.rationale: Its Prisma schema uses Json columns that SQLite does not support, so unlike PEDIDO it can never be downgraded to SQLite.

nodes.label: Build normal bajo PM2 (evitar warning de output: standalone)
nodes.rationale: standalone output is only for Docker; under PM2 the app is started with next start, and a standalone build spams delivery-error.log with a cosmetic warning that hides real errors.

nodes.label: config.json con el sucursalId REAL de esta instalación
nodes.rationale: Copying the file from another install points at an id that does not exist in this database, and the integration silently returns 0 orders.

nodes.label: pm2 save tras añadir procesos
nodes.rationale: Unsaved processes vanish on a daemon restart or pm2 resurrect, which is how the sync worker silently disappears.
